title: Context Matters, Doesn't It? The Role of Context in Everyday Emotion Regulation Strategy Use.
abstract: A common maxim holds that "context is everything." This perspective transformed the field of emotion regulation, which evolved from understandingregulation strategies people use, to understandingstrategy use varies by context (i.e., strategy-situation fit). Theoretical accounts suggest contextual features are crucial in guiding strategy use. However, empirical evidence is isolated in piecemeal studies with inconclusive results. To comprehensively explore context-dependent emotion regulation, we need data on emotion regulation across many contexts, at scale. Combining up to 11 experience-sampling data sets collected from Belgian and Australian samples in an integrative analysis (= 500-1,696,= 27,023-101,114,= 25.38 years, 71% women), we examined how regulation-strategy use varies as a function of three theory-derived contextual features-,, and(i.e., the presence and closeness of others). We found limited support that context matters for daily emotion-regulation strategy use. Our study provides a well-powered foundational step to test a theory central to emotion-regulation research and highlights the complexity of capturing strategy-situation fit in daily life.
